title: KV-Cache Patching: Tracing How and Where Fine-Tuned Behaviors Arise
summary: The technique replaces direct fine-tuning or full model switching by patching key-value (KV) cache states from a fine-tuned model into a base model (or vice versa) to transfer specific behaviors like language switching or misalignment. It costs inference-time computation for cache manipulation and adds complexity in identifying pivotal token positions, with no training required but potential latency overhead during cache swapping. Failures include inconsistent behavior transfer if patched positions are not pivotal, reliance on attention mechanisms that may not generalize across prompts, and inability to fully replicate or remove fine-tuned behaviors in all cases.
rationale: This method enables lightweight behavior adaptation on constrained infrastructure without model retraining, but requires empirical validation for specific use cases due to variability in effectiveness and dependence on cache position influence.
